name: Twisted Metal: Head-On - Extra Twisted Edition PC Port

inputs.label: Your disc image (.iso) of Twisted Metal: Head-On - Extra Twisted Edition, the USA PlayStation 2 release, serial SCUS-97621.

actions.label: Saves
actions.help: The memory cards (mc0 and mc1) your saves are on.

actions.label: Screenshots
actions.help: The pictures F12 takes in the game.

actions.label: Logs
actions.help: The performance and graphics logs, for bug reports.

exit_codes.21: Your disc image couldn't be opened or read: it may have been moved, deleted or damaged. Pick it again on the game's page.
exit_codes.22: That disc image isn't Twisted Metal: Head-On - Extra Twisted Edition (USA, SCUS-97621). Pick that game's disc image on the game's page.
exit_codes.23: The game couldn't copy its program from your disc image into its folder. Check that the drive has free space and the folder isn't read-only.

settings.label: Display mode
settings.help: Windowed, borderless full screen, or exclusive full screen. F11 or Alt+Enter switches in the game too.

settings.label: Resolution
settings.help: The game picture's resolution, whatever your screen is. 480p is the PS2's own; higher is sharper and harder on the graphics card.

settings.label: Aspect ratio
settings.help: 4:3 is the original picture. 16:9 is true widescreen: the cameras see more to each side, and the HUD and text keep their shape.

settings.label: Scaling
settings.help: How the picture is enlarged to your screen: Sharp keeps square pixels, Smooth uses a sharp Lanczos filter.

settings.label: Frame rate
settings.help: 60 fps (recommended) shows the game's own frames, and on Windows Lossless Scaling's frame generation makes it smoothest; 120 fps and Monitor add the port's own in-between frames instead.

settings.label: V-Sync
settings.help: Waits for the monitor's refresh to avoid tearing.

settings.label: Brightness
settings.help: 100 is the game's own picture. Dark parts change most, so night arenas get easier to see.

settings.label: Sharpening
settings.help: Makes fine detail and text crisper after the picture is scaled. 0 leaves the picture as it is.

settings.label: Intro movies
settings.help: The logo and intro movies when the game starts. The intro can still be watched from the game's own menus.

settings.label: Controller vibration
settings.help: Lets the game rumble your controller when you hit or get hit, as on the PS2.

settings.label: Pause on controller loss
settings.help: Pauses the game and opens its menu when the controller you play with disconnects.

settings.label: FPS counter
settings.help: Shows the frames per second in a corner of the game.

settings.label: Camera distance
settings.help: How far the chase camera sits behind your car, in percent: 100 is the game's own.

settings.label: Camera angle
settings.help: How high the chase camera looks down at your car, in degrees: 0 is the game's own.

settings.label: Field of view
settings.help: How wide the battle camera sees. The game's own is 65° at 4:3 and 81° at 16:9.

settings.label: Master volume
settings.help: Volume of everything the game plays.

settings.label: Music volume
settings.help: The music in menus and battles.

settings.label: Effects volume
settings.help: Engines, weapons, explosions, pickups, menu sounds and the announcer.

settings.label: Movie volume
settings.help: The sound of the intro and ending movies.

settings.label: Mute in background
settings.help: Silences the game while its window isn't in front.

settings.label: Renderer
settings.help: Vulkan draws the game on your graphics card; Software uses the CPU and is much slower.
